blocks.description: Sets whether new peer connections use LAN-only ICE or public STUN servers.
Creates a manual pairing offer code for the named peer.
Returns the latest offer code generated for the named peer.
Accepts a peer's offer code and creates an answer code.
Returns the latest answer code generated for the named peer.
Completes pairing by accepting a peer's answer code.

blocks.text: send event [TYPE] payload [PAYLOAD] channel [CHANNEL] to peer [PEER]
blocks.description: Sends a JSON event envelope to one peer, or to all peers when PEER is *.
Opts in or out of unreliable latest-data channels. The default is disabled.

blocks.text: configure latest-data channel [CHANNEL] high-water mark [HIGH_WATER_MARK] bytes for peer [PEER]
blocks.description: Configures a named latest-data channel before creating an offer.

blocks.text: send latest data [PAYLOAD] channel [CHANNEL] to peer [PEER]
blocks.description: Sends without waiting, or drops the new value when bufferedAmount exceeds the high-water mark.

blocks.text: latest-data buffered bytes for channel [CHANNEL] peer [PEER]
blocks.description: Returns the browser DataChannel bufferedAmount for a named latest-data channel.

blocks.text: latest-data sent count for channel [CHANNEL] peer [PEER]
blocks.description: Returns the number of values handed to the named latest-data channel.

blocks.text: latest-data dropped count for channel [CHANNEL] peer [PEER]
blocks.description: Returns the number of new values dropped by backpressure.
Returns disabled, not-configured, connecting, open, closing, or closed.
Returns the fixed backpressure policy, drop-newest.
Returns the version of the runtime API for composite extensions.
Throws an explicit error when the requested runtime API version is unsupported.

blocks.text: broadcast network message [MESSAGE] payload [PAYLOAD] channel [CHANNEL] to peer [PEER]
blocks.description: Sends a network broadcast message envelope to one peer, or to all peers when PEER is *.
Starts scripts when a matching network broadcast message is received.
Returns the payload of the most recently received network broadcast message as JSON.
Returns the sender ID of the most recently received network broadcast message.
Returns the local peer name that received the most recent network broadcast message.
Returns the channel of the most recently received network broadcast message.
Reports whether the receive queue contains at least one message.
Returns the number of messages currently waiting in the receive queue.
Removes and returns the oldest received message as JSON.
Returns the most recent received message as JSON without removing it.
Clears the receive queue.
Returns the WebRTC connection state for the named peer.
Returns a JSON array of connected peer names.
Closes and removes a peer connection.
Runs a clock probe exchange with the peer and stores the resulting clock offset.
Returns the microseconds to add to a local timestamp to express it in the peer's clock.

blocks.text: clock round trip to peer [PEER] us
blocks.description: Returns the shortest round trip observed while probing the peer, in microseconds.
Returns the clock offset uncertainty for the peer in microseconds, which is half the shortest round trip.

blocks.text: time in clock of peer [PEER] us
blocks.description: Returns the current local time expressed in the peer's clock, in microseconds. Errors when the peer clock has not been probed yet.
Returns the local high-resolution clock in microseconds.

blocks.text: frame latency us for capture [CAPTURE_US] pattern [PATTERN_US] wrap [WRAP_US] from peer [PEER]
blocks.description: Returns how many microseconds after the displayed pattern time the local frame was captured. CAPTURE_US is a local timestamp, PATTERN_US is the decoded display time in the peer's clock, and WRAP_US is the pattern repeat period, or 0 when the pattern never repeats. Errors when the peer clock has not been probed yet. A negative result means the clock offset or the frame age correction exceeded the real latency.

blocks.text: record frame sync sample for camera [CAMERA] capture [CAPTURE_US] pattern [PATTERN_US] wrap [WRAP_US] from peer [PEER]
blocks.description: Converts one pattern observation into a latency sample and stores it for the camera slot. Errors when the peer clock has not been probed yet.

blocks.text: clear frame sync samples for camera [CAMERA]
blocks.description: Clears the latency samples stored for the camera slot.

blocks.text: frame sync sample count for camera [CAMERA]
blocks.description: Returns how many latency samples are stored for the camera slot.
Returns the local latency summary for the camera slot as a JSON report.

blocks.text: send frame sync report for camera [CAMERA] to peer [PEER]
blocks.description: Sends the camera slot's latency summary to the peer on the internal sync channel.
Returns every received frame sync report together with per-camera offsets as JSON.
Returns a JSON array of the camera slots that have reported.

blocks.text: frame sync latency us of camera [CAMERA]
blocks.description: Returns the reported median capture latency of the camera slot in microseconds.

blocks.text: frame sync offset us of camera [CAMERA]
blocks.description: Returns how many microseconds later than the reference camera this camera finishes recording a frame. Subtract it from the camera's frame timestamps to align the cameras.
Clears every received frame sync report.
